\## Overview

This document describes Script 0 of the ATAC-seq and RNA-seq integration

pipeline for the chicken embryo antagomir study. Script 0 corrects the fold

change direction in the six raw DiffBind ATAC-seq output files, standardises

column names to DESeq2 convention, and saves both full corrected and

significance-filtered versions for downstream analysis.

\### The problem

DiffBind calculates \`Fold\` as log2(Group2/Group1) --- where Group2 is the

second-named group in the filename --- instead of the expected

log2(Group1/Group2). This means that for a file named

\`DEseq2_AM133_v_AMScr.tsv\`, a positive \`Fold\` value indicates greater

chromatin accessibility in AMScr (Group2), not AM133 (Group1). If used

uncorrected, all concordance classifications in the integration step would

be biologically reversed.

\### The solution

Five of the six files are corrected by multiplying \`Fold\` by -1. The sixth

file (\`DEseq2_AM1_206_v_AM133.tsv\`) already has the correct direction ---

positive \`Fold\` means higher accessibility in AM133 --- which matches the

corresponding RNA-seq file (\`AM133vsAM1_206_deg_all.tsv\`). This file is

renamed only, to reflect its true biological direction.

\### Column standardisation

All six files have columns renamed to match DESeq2 convention:

\| Original name \| New name \| Reason \|

\|\-\--\|\-\--\|\-\--\|

\| \`Fold\` \| \`log2FoldChange\` \| Standard DESeq2 naming \|

\| \`FDR\` \| \`padj\` \| Standard adjusted p-value name \|

\| \`p-value\` \| \`pvalue\` \| Removes hyphen to avoid R syntax issues \|

\## Results

\### Correction summary

\| Comparison \| Action \| Total peaks \| Significant (padj \<= 0.05) \| % \|

\|\-\--\|\-\--\|\-\--\|\-\--\|\-\--\|

\| AM133_vs_AMScr \| Flipped + renamed \| 93,678 \| 10,652 \| 11.4% \|

\| AMAll_vs_AMScr \| Flipped + renamed \| 92,751 \| 13,388 \| 14.4% \|

\| AM1_206_vs_AMScr \| Flipped + renamed \| 95,911 \| 132 \| 0.1% \|

\| AM133_vs_AM1_206 \| Renamed only \| 79,564 \| 1,969 \| 2.5% \|

\| AM133_vs_AMAll \| Flipped + renamed \| 71,670 \| 9 \| 0.0% \|

\| AM1_206_vs_AMAll \| Flipped + renamed \| 78,038 \| 6,685 \| 8.6% \|

\### Meaning of positive log2FoldChange after correction

\| Comparison \| Positive log2FoldChange means \|

\|\-\--\|\-\--\|

\| AM133_vs_AMScr \| More open in AM133 \|

\| AMAll_vs_AMScr \| More open in AMAll \|

\| AM1_206_vs_AMScr \| More open in AM1/206 \|

\| AM133_vs_AM1_206 \| More open in AM133 \|

\| AM133_vs_AMAll \| More open in AM133 \|

\| AM1_206_vs_AMAll \| More open in AM1/206 \|

\### Verification

All six files were verified before and after correction using the \`Conc\`

columns as ground truth. For each file, a test peak was identified where

the first-named group had at least 2x higher mean chromatin accessibility

concentration than the second-named group. Before correction, this peak

had a negative \`log2FoldChange\` in the five flipped files --- confirming the

direction was reversed. After correction, the same peak showed a positive

\`log2FoldChange\` with exactly opposite sign --- confirming the flip was

applied correctly. For the renamed-only file (AM133_vs_AM1_206), the test

peak had a positive \`log2FoldChange\` both before and after --- confirming

the direction was already correct.
